Analysis

Hypothesis — stage-level provenance will become a more useful comparison than a binary human/synthetic label. The sample already contains human-authored preferences, model-generated feedback, synthetic educational scores and human correction of model responses. Confidence is moderate for the usefulness of this distinction and unestablished for its effect on procurement outcomes. The hypothesis would strengthen if provenance-complete manifests predict fewer acceptance surprises on matched tasks; it would weaken if those details fail to add information beyond ordinary samples and contracts. This is a research proposition, not a forecast of market adoption.

Evidence: candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels, next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback, candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels, cohort5.claim.deepseekv3.human-check

Analysis

Hypothesis — environment and verifier maintenance will be a distinct recurring delivery burden. Refresh describes versioned verifiers, OSWorld announces a verified-version change, and SWE-bench Multimodal reports repeated-test filtering. Confidence is moderate that version and stability matter within these examples, but the corpus supplies no market-wide maintenance cost. A longitudinal study should record environment breakage, verifier corrections and acceptance changes under frozen agents. If stable tasks require little upkeep across relevant software changes, the hypothesized burden would be narrower than suggested.

Evidence: candidate.cohort4.refresh.versioned-verifiers, cohort4.dataset.claim.osworld.version-change, cohort6.claim.swemultimodal.stability-appendix

Analysis

Hypothesis — multilingual validity will require native task design as well as translation quality. M-IFEval modifies constraints, MENLO isolates local dimensions and BenchMAX post-edits translated data. Confidence is moderate for the methodological distinction, without an estimated commercial premium. A useful experiment would match translated, post-edited and native-authored tasks on intended constructs and independently score local failures. Equal validity under those controlled conditions would weaken the need for a separate native-authoring stage in that particular use case.

Evidence: cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter, cohort7.claim.mifeval.objective, cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions, cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline

Analysis

Hypothesis — reliability reporting will need both repeated execution and disagreement preservation. τ-bench distinguishes all-trials reliability from at-least-one success, while DICES and the disagreement study expose meaningful variation in human labels. Confidence is high that these are different denominators; the effect on supplier selection remains untested. A matched pilot should compare decisions made from aggregate success alone with decisions using repeated trials, raw labels and adjudication reasons. The hypothesis would weaken if added detail does not change acceptance or predict deployment errors.

Evidence: cohort4.claim.taubench.repeat-reliability, cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference, cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement

Analysis

Hypothesis — reward-model and monitor evaluations will need adversarial separation from the optimization loop. Summarization overoptimization, verifier search exploitation and the reasoning-monitor study demonstrate specific mechanisms by which optimization can outpace a proxy. Confidence is moderate for the need to test this risk, not for its prevalence in current services. Hold out failure classes and reviewer inputs when optimizing the system, then measure independent outcome errors. A robust matched study showing stable external validity across optimization intensity would narrow this concern.

Evidence: cohort3.claim.summarize.overoptimization, cohort2.claim.verifiers.search-limit, cohort7.claim.monitor.optimization

Analysis

Hypothesis — labor and documentation quality should be evaluated as operating processes, not only disclosure artifacts. CrowdWorkSheets asks for maintenance and pool-selection rationale; Datasheets asks about collection participants and compensation; the labor study warns about unknown population boundaries. Confidence is moderate for the research value of these fields, with no causal claim that publishing them improves wages or model quality. Follow-up research should compare documentation with consented worker evidence and project logs, retaining discrepancies and avoiding a disclosure-completeness score that masquerades as performance.

Evidence: cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.maintenance, cohort8.claim.crowdworksheets.selection-rationale, candidate.paperfull.datasheets.worker-compensation-disclosure, cohort8.claim.latinlabour.representativeness

Research gap

Priority evidence gaps: comparable accepted-unit economics; contributor-level paid-active windows; independent project outcomes; version-specific rights clearance; non-English and non-text coverage intersections; benchmark side-effect detection; and a complete source-supported supplier contribution map. The current graph’s richer catalogue does not resolve these automatically. Research should prioritize decision-changing evidence rather than optimize counts, and should document negative findings and unresolved cases alongside additions.

Method

The weekly outlook should be revised through falsifiable change conditions. Each stable executive finding records confidence, reasoning, limitations and what would change the assessment. New primary evidence can strengthen, narrow or supersede a finding; a changed source version should not silently overwrite its predecessor. A meaningful revision will identify which observed assumption changed and whether the effect is task-specific or supports a broader conclusion. No growth, revenue, employment or technology-adoption forecast is produced from this selected corpus.

Analysis

Hypothesis — a stronger documentation audit will improve diligence only if reporting signals are checked against project evidence. GIGO and Who Annotates observe disclosure, not undisclosed practice; the latter also exposes extraction uncertainty. Confidence is moderate in the need to distinguish those objects and unmeasured in the commercial value of an audit score. A follow-up could compare disclosed instructions, training and compensation fields with consented project records and independently sampled outputs. If completeness fails to predict agreement between disclosure and practice, its role should remain a transparency measure rather than a performance proxy.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.gigo.audit-limit, repair20261111.claim.current-reference045, cohort9.claim.whoannotates.audit-limit, cohort9.claim.whoannotates.reporting-pattern

Analysis

Hypothesis — complete-task reliability will be more decision-relevant than fractional rubric completion in workflows with decisive controls. APEX-Accounting, HANDBOOK.md and DAYJOB distinguish strict/relaxed or mean-criterion/repeated-complete metrics; PLE’s hybrid score exposes a different tradeoff. Confidence is moderate in the hypothesis and high that the metrics differ. A prospective workflow study should compare acceptance and downstream failure predicted by each metric under a fixed task population. If fractional scores predict accepted outcomes as well after severity and review costs are controlled, the proposed emphasis should narrow.

Analysis

Hypothesis — purported transfer mechanisms will become clearer when data design is treated as an experimental treatment. The connected office-work studies generate descriptive transfer and trace hypotheses; Corecraft and the coding-task study add different recipes and baseline conditions. Confidence is low in a shared causal explanation from these reports. A multi-seed, equal-budget factorial study separating task domain, demonstration quality, reward shaping and base-model choice could strengthen a particular mechanism. Null or domain-specific findings would weaken broad claims that one data category generalizes across professional work.

Analysis

Hypothesis — disclosure of excluded work and selected populations will improve procurement decisions more than larger raw row counts. Qualification self-selection, disagreement filtering, adversarial task screening and translated rows all change the effective denominator in the reviewed studies. Confidence is moderate in the decision relevance and unmeasured in commercial impact. A blinded buyer study could compare choices made from headline totals with choices made from full admission/exclusion manifests, then validate the selected service on independent work. No effect on selection accuracy or accepted cost would narrow this hypothesis.

Analysis

Hypothesis — benchmark maintenance will become a separate recurring research and procurement cost. SWE Atlas changes grading while retaining tasks; MMLU-Pro corrects answers and whitespace; ProgramBench has paper/card difficulty differences; TH1.1 changes tasks and human-time estimates as well as infrastructure. Confidence is moderate in the maintenance-burden hypothesis and high that these are real version distinctions. A prospective cost ledger should compare revalidation, regrading and downstream decision changes under frozen versus updated protocols. If stable old protocols predict accepted outcomes equally well, the proposed maintenance premium should narrow.

Analysis

Testable judgment — release evolution can alter a score without a new logical family. AA-LCR repairs answer keys and warns against direct score comparison; DecoyCount distinguishes release withdrawals, stale derived answers and historical scores; Harvey LAB changes task rosters; DeepResearch Bench II changes the scored subset and judge protocol. The proposed hypothesis is that a meaningful portion of apparent score movement in an evolving evaluation could arise from these protocol or population changes. No fraction is estimated here. Confidence is high that matched-version replay is necessary and unknown about the contribution of each factor. Re-evaluating unchanged stored outputs under old/new scorers, then rerunning a fixed task intersection under fixed scaffolds, would separate these explanations.

Evidence: candidate.third11.aa-lcr.version.v2, candidate.next12.decoycount.derived-answer-limit.v2, candidate.next12.decoycount.release-units.v3, candidate.third11.harvey-lab.release-scope.v2, candidate.third11.deepresearch.evaluation-evolution.v2, candidate.third11.deepresearch.units-and-current-scope.v2

Analysis

Testable judgment — downstream improvement needs a controlled training contrast rather than a promising environment specification. PostTrain Arena describes a fixed before/after held-out comparison, but its captured landing state pauses challenge runs and its later README distinguishes bounded pipeline checks from a completed held-out training run. The implication is methodological: freeze base model, compute, recipe, held-out suite and acceptance rules, then report repeated-run uncertainty before attributing a gain to contributed environments. This report asserts no completed PostTrain gain or supplier ranking. Confidence is high in the documented distinction and unknown for the intended program’s effectiveness. Actual accepted held-out runs with matched controls would supply the evidence that changes it.

Evidence: candidate.add17.posttrain.demonstration-limits.v2, candidate.add17.posttrain.fixed-comparison.v2, candidate.add17.posttrain.quality-gates.v2
